Approval is blocked by semantic contradiction, omission, and grounding defects. The candidate says authorization is unspecified even though both edit examples show an Authorization: Bearer header. It says the second request replaces applicable_product_ids although the guide demonstrates the resulting two-product applicability without defining general array replacement semantics. It repeats updateEndDate without noting that the dedicated get-edit-history reference names updateContractEndDate. It also repeats the guide's claim that the first edit's created_at is passed as as_of_date even though the shown edit records expose timestamp, not created_at, and the displayed historical contract state's created_at predates the first edit; the request itself is not shown, so the exact timestamp source is unresolved. The shared customers-and-contracts update omits the guide's durable getContract as_of_date historical-state route and its statement that all edits also enter UI/API audit logs, and it would introduce the unqualified updateEndDate name into canonical concept prose. Grounding is incomplete: quote 1 omits the detailed first edit payload asserted by the candidate, quote 2 claims lines 108-124 but contains only line 108 and therefore omits the finalized-February and void/regenerate behavior, and quote 3 omits the edit records, as_of_date historical state, and audit-log statement asserted by the candidate. These semantic and evidence corrections require another complete-source review.

Full-source review found the query inventory itself accurate. The candidate correctly covers non-archived customers, monthly event counts, invoice and line-item aggregation, daily draft snapshots, global-maximum snapshot selection, ID-plus-snapshot breakdown joins, Production-only breakdown examples, exclusion of negative aggregate line items, archived contracts, descending override ordering without a one-row limit, future-ending rate-card entries, active webhook-alert predicates, and alert-history grouping. It also correctly identifies three defects in the raw cookbook: the Finalized Invoices queries have no status predicate although the database reference says invoice contains both FINALIZED and VOID rows; the query titled over the last week has no time predicate; and the detailed draft-breakdown query selects six nonaggregated expressions while grouping by only two despite the standard-SQL framing. Its universal-divide-by-100 caution is directionally correct. Approval is nevertheless blocked by material table-grain and aggregation omissions exposed by the already-ingested export authorities. Metronome configures one export destination across Production and Sandbox, but outside the two breakdown examples most cookbook queries do not filter environment_type; their counts and monetary totals therefore cannot be presented as environment-scoped without an explicit filter. Object-storage exports are append-only and at-least-once and incremental consumers must resolve repeated primary keys to the latest row, yet none of the cookbook queries performs delivery deduplication. A global maximum snapshot_time or snapshot_timestamp is also not a per-object latest-row or completeness guarantee. The draft_invoice reference permits DRAFT_INCOMPLETE rows with no total or line items, so COUNT can include incomplete invoices while SUM ignores null totals unless status/completeness is handled. The active-rate-card-entry query checks only ending_before greater than NOW(): it does not check starting_at, does not define how nullable ending_before behaves, and does not select among version or snapshot rows, so it is not a complete active-entry count. The candidate's generic lifecycle and duplicate-handling sentence is too weak for these documented cross-source boundaries, while the proposed query-patterns update would canonize the patterns without their necessary environment, deduplication, incomplete-draft, and version-selection qualifications. Finally, total/100 is not a universal fiat conversion under the existing Metronome currency authority, but the candidate and shared update do not link that direct authority. Mechanical checks pass: the trusted raw SHA-256, canonical URL, raw_files value, source target state, and exact path-qualified raw backlink are correct; no duplicate canonical source exists; candidate.md equals receipt.source_page; suggestions.json equals receipt.suggestions; all five grounding excerpts byte-match their cited raw spans; and the selected reporting concept is the correct authority. These semantic and cross-source corrections require another full-source review.
